title: Benchmark harness integration - edge cases & success criteria
summary: POC scoping for benchmark harness integration. Covered customer scripts, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, target QPS/latency SLOs, telemetry points to capture, required security artifacts and timeline for a Jan pilot. Agreed next steps: share annotated harness template, run two-week pilot focusing on 5k QPS synthetic + 1m-per-day real traffic replay, and schedule follow-up for results review.
next_steps: Redwood to send annotated harness repo + example customer script (Maya) by 2026-01-02
Customer to provide representative prompt set and 48h sample logs (Sara) by 2026-01-05
Schedule latency-focused pilot run window Jan 8-10, 2026 (all)
Exchange security checklist and SOC2 attestation docs (Ellen/Maya) by 2026-01-03
action_items: Maya Patel; Send annotated harness template and README with streaming examples; 2026-01-02
Diego Alvarez; Prepare default load profile (streaming and non-streaming) and expected P95/P99 baselines; 2026-01-06
Sara Collins; Export 24-48h sample prompts + traffic distribution histogram; 2026-01-05
Ellen Park; Confirm data residency and KMS requirements and share redacted audit scope; 2026-01-03
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off, quick intros. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. Diego is our SE and Priya CSM.
[00:12] Sara Collins: Hi, Sara here, head of ML at ArcadiaHealth. We've got Raj and Ellen on from platform and security and Tom from SRE. Thanks for fitting us in.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: Great, thanks. Today we want to scope the benchmark/poc harness integration: success criteria, what scripts you have, streaming vs non-streaming behavior, and timeline.
[00:35] Raj Mehta: Quick context — we run a mix of real-time chat flows and batch summarization jobs. Realtime is low-latency, ~200ms target; batch jobs are throughput focused. We'll need both in the POC.
[00:50] Ellen Park: Security first: we need to validate data retention, KMS integration, and audit logs. We'll need SOC2 docs and a basic network diagram.
[01:03] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll attach SOC2 and a high-level network diagram. For the harness: do you have existing scripts or do you want Redwood's adapter?
[01:14] Sara Collins: We have a Python-based load harness that replays logged traffic and a Node script for streaming chat tests. They're not standardized and missing error injection.
[01:26] Diego Alvarez: OK. Typical approach: we provide an annotated harness repo and a small adapter your team drops in — it converts your prompt/response schema to the harness format and the harness can run streaming and non-streaming scenarios.
[01:39] Tom Li: Streaming is tricky for us — we care about tail latency and broken partial responses. How does the harness surface partial frame errors?
[01:49] Diego Alvarez: We'll instrument with per-chunk latencies, aggregate P50/P95/P99 and also emit event traces when incomplete deltas appear. The harness can replay both full-response and chunked streaming to simulate browser clients.
[02:02] Sara Collins: Success criteria — what we expect: P95 latency < 300ms for short chat prompts, P99 under 800ms; for batch summarization we want throughput > 200 req/s for 8k token average. Also model accuracy regression under 2% mismatch to our baseline.
[02:20] Maya Patel: Nice — we'll capture those as acceptance tests. For accuracy regression you have an eval set?
[02:28] Sara Collins: Yes, we have a 2k-sample prompt-eval set, and a quality rubric. We'll provide it.
[02:34] Diego Alvarez: On workload sizing, Raj — can you share QPS distribution?
[02:38] Raj Mehta: Our 24h peak is ~5k QPS for lightweight prompts, 1k QPS sustained for heavier flows. But in production we're mostly mixing — roughly 70% short chat, 30% long batch.
[02:52] Diego Alvarez: Good, that'll inform batching policies and GPU sizing. For the POC pilot we'll synthetic-load to 5k QPS and run a traffic-replay of 24-48h sample at 1x.
[03:03] Maya Patel: Timeline check — you're hoping for a pilot before end of January?
[03:07] Sara Collins: Yes, ideally mid-Jan so internal stakeholders can review before Feb budget cycle.
[03:12] Diego Alvarez: We can target Jan 8-10 for a latency-focused run and Jan 15-22 for a scale/stability window.
[03:20] Ellen Park: On security, we need to know where logs live and who has access. Also KMS key policies — customer-managed KMS is a requirement for production.
[03:32] Maya Patel: Redwood Private supports customer KMS; for hosted POC we can use temporary envelope encryption with limited retention and provide audit logs. We'll send a checklist.
[03:43] Raj Mehta: What about model variants and fallbacks? We need deterministic fallback policies.
[03:48] Diego Alvarez: The harness will run fallback scenarios: model A slower, fallback to model B (smaller) — and we can capture end-to-end correctness and latency delta. We'll also run A/B baseline comparisons.
[04:00] Tom Li: Instrumentation — can we get token-level logs? SRE needs token counts and per-token latencies to reconcile cost.
[04:07] Diego Alvarez: Yes, token counts and cost estimates can be output per request. We also provide routing logs and KV cache hit rates if you enable prefix caching.
[04:19] Sara Collins: A couple of edge cases: malformed prompts that cause model hangs, and long-running streams that drop mid-sequence. Can we simulate network flakiness?
[04:30] Diego Alvarez: We can inject network latency and TCP resets in the harness. For hangs we can set a watchdog and capture partial outputs; we'll include a scenario that times out after configurable thresholds.
[04:43] Maya Patel: Ok, recap — deliverables from Redwood: annotated harness repo with streaming & non-streaming examples, default load profiles, a runbook for the Jan pilot, and security attestation docs.
[04:55] Sara Collins: From us: sample prompts, 24-48h logs, a list of acceptance criteria owners, and a test account for the pilot.
[05:05] Priya Narang: Quick note — CSM will own coordination; we'll schedule daily stand-ups during pilot window.
[05:12] Raj Mehta: One more: telemetry retention. We'll need raw traces for 14 days and aggregated metrics for 90 days. Is that configurable?
[05:20] Diego Alvarez: Yes, retention tiers are configurable; for POC we'll keep raw traces for 14 days and push aggregated to your Grafana. We'll share export endpoints.
[05:30] Ellen Park: Compliance — can you confirm no PII is stored during the POC? We may need to sanitize logs.
[05:36] Maya Patel: We recommend redaction at ingestion. We can provide a sanitizer script as part of the harness and show how to toggle it.
[05:45] Tom Li: During the last internal run we saw a tokenization mismatch that skewed cost estimates. How do you handle tokenizer differences between models?
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: Harness can normalize tokenization by running the tokenizers client-side and attaching canonical token counts. We'll include that in the adapter examples.
[06:05] Sara Collins: Timeline/agreement — we need a short SOW for the POC outlining success criteria and what triggers a paid pilot.
[06:13] Maya Patel: We'll produce a one-page SOW after this call and attach success criteria items.
[06:18] Priya Narang: I'll set up the Jan 8-10 pilot calendar invite and daily syncs.
[06:24] Maya Patel: Any blockers?
[06:26] Ellen Park: Nothing immediate — just waiting on the security checklist and KMS confirmation.
[06:30] Raj Mehta: We'll prioritize extracting the 48h sample logs.
[06:34] Maya Patel: Perfect. We'll send the harness link and a skeleton script.
[06:38] Sara Collins: One last Q — for streaming vs non-streaming, what's your recommended approach for spending our credits during the pilot? We want to avoid burning excessive tokens.
[06:49] Diego Alvarez: Start with scaled-down streaming for correctness and then escalate to full QPS for short bursts. Use prefix caching and response chunking to save costs during large replays. We'll provide cost knobs in the runbook.
[07:02] Tom Li: Good. Let's wrap.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts and the SOW. Meeting adjourned.
[07:10] (call ends)
